title: Removing access barriers to children and adolescent rehabilitation
summary:
Medical rehabilitation for children and adolescents (child and adolescent rehab) in Germany usually consists of a four-week program designed to improve the health of children and adolescents with a chronic condition, for example neurodermatitis or bronchial asthma. Rehabilitation for children and adolescents is predominantly financed by the statutory German Pension Insurance (GPI) or the statutory health insurance providers. 
Although the frequency of chronic conditions in children has not decreased in recent years, the number of people insured with the GPI applying for medical rehabilitation for their child is decreasing. The ‘ReACh-Rehab’ project is designed to change this.  Four components are therefore being developed in ReACh-Rehab to help increase the number of applications. These four components are being implemented in the federal states in which GPI North is operating. These are Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Schleswig-Holstein (model region).
The first component is the development and introduction of a shortened application form. Thereby it is intended to make it easier for parents as well as physicians to fill out the application. Secondly, for the duration of the project, the GPI will inform medical practices, schools, daycare centers and other places where parents can be encountered about the possibility of child and adolescent rehab and advise interested parties on how to apply. The third component is the so-called rehab coaching. The rehab coaching is implemented by our cooperation partner, the Ethno-Medical Center e. V. (EMZ). In this module, the coaches trained by the EMZ support families in the application process, answer questions about child and adolescent rehab and help with the compilation of the necessary documents (e.g. obtaining a report from the pediatrician). In addition, as a fourth component, we will also provide a website for child and adolescent rehab that offers parents, doctors and other interested parties all the necessary information from the application process to implementation and aftercare following completion of child and adolescent rehab. 
We use various methods to investigate how well these four components are implemented and whether the implemented interventions lead to an increase in applications for CAR. We conduct interviews with parents, physicians and GPI employees to find out how satisfied they are with the current application form for child and adolescents rehabilitation and to determine which changes they consider necessary. In addition, we are surveying parents who have made the previous application with a questionnaire about their experiences with the application form and the application process. 
The same questionnaire will later be used to survey parents who have used the new shortened application form. This will enable us to compare the results of the surveys and assess whether the new application form performs better. 
Furthermore, we use interviews and questionnaires to understand how participants experience our advisory, information and coaching services for child and adolescent rehab. For example, we ask how satisfied they are with the amount of time spent coaching, whether the coach was able to help them sufficiently and whether they would recommend the coaching to others.
This way, we will learn how the four components are accepted by the participants and whether they perceive them to be effective or not. However, at the end of our project, we also would like to determine whether these four components of the program genuinely lead to an increase in applications for child and youth rehabilitation at the GPI. To investigate this, we will receive anonymized data from the GPI on all applications submitted for CAR in the period from 2024 to 2026. We will examine whether the number of applications has changed favorably over the years since the introduction of our four components. To ensure that this development is related to the components of our project and is not influenced by Germany-wide developments, such as a change in chronic diseases, we also compare the development in our model region with a control region. This approach is called a difference-in-difference analysis, as we compare the difference in our model region with the difference in the other region.

The control group comprises individuals insured by the German Pension Insurance who live in Berlin or Brandenburg. This region is located outside the implementation region of the intervention and represents the reference region in the difference-in-differences analyses.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Persons insured with the German Pension Insurance residing in Hamburg, Mecklenburg- Vorpommern, Schleswig-Holstein or Berlin and Brandenburg with an application for children and adolescents rehabilitation according to § 15a SGB VI in 2024, 2025 or 2026 deposited in the insured person's account.
Exclusion criteria:
None
